findings.issue: consumeAuthState() is a destructive one-time sessionStorage read invoked synchronously at the top of the async run() function, inside a useEffect that mounts under React.StrictMode (client/src/main.jsx:7 wraps the app in <React.StrictMode>). StrictMode double-invokes effects in dev (mount -> cleanup -> mount). The first invocation of run() executes synchronously through consumeAuthState() (deletes the sessionStorage key) before the first `await`, then gets cleaned up (isActive=false) by React's synchronous remount; the async exchangeYandexCode() call in that first invocation still completes for real later (the unconditional `window.location.replace(...)` on line 51 is not gated by isActive) and will redirect away. The second, 'real' invocation calls consumeAuthState() again, finds the key already gone, and immediately (synchronously) calls finalize("error"), rendering 'Ошибка авторизации' for that instance.
findings.impact: Every time a developer or QA tester logs in against the dev server (exactly the environment the task's own Verification Steps specify: localhost:5173) they will see a guaranteed, deterministic 'Ошибка авторизации' flash immediately followed by the real success redirect. This is dev-only (StrictMode double-invoke does not happen in production builds), so it will not affect real users, but it directly collides with the task's prescribed manual verification flow ('Выйти и войти заново → вход проходит успешно') and can be mistaken for a genuine regression, wasting QA time or masking a real bug behind expected noise. It is also a strictly more deterministic failure mode than the pre-existing StrictMode double-exchangeYandexCode race that existed before this task (previously both instances tried to exchange the same one-time code and typically only one succeeded, depending on server timing).
findings.recommendation: Guard the whole run() body with a ref-based single-execution flag (e.g. `const ranRef = useRef(false); if (ranRef.current) return; ranRef.current = true;` set at the very top of the effect, reset is unnecessary since AuthCallback mounts once per real navigation) so the second StrictMode invocation is a true no-op instead of re-running the state comparison against an already-consumed value. This is the standard fix for 'effect must run its side effect exactly once' code under StrictMode.

findings.issue: createAuthState()'s fallback path calls `window.crypto.getRandomValues(bytes)` without an existence guard on `window.crypto` itself — only `window.crypto?.randomUUID` is optionally-chained, not the fallback access. If `window.crypto` is undefined (very old/unusual browser or embedded webview lacking the Crypto API entirely), this throws a TypeError. buildYandexAuthUrl (which calls createAuthState synchronously) is invoked directly from AuthModal.jsx:9's onClick handler with no try/catch around it, so the exception would propagate uncaught out of a React event handler.
findings.impact: On a browser lacking `window.crypto` entirely, clicking 'Войти с Яндекс ID' throws instead of failing gracefully (contrast with buildYandexAuthUrl's own existing `if (!clientId) return null` graceful-degradation pattern one function down). Low real-world likelihood given the project's Vite browser target, but it is a newly-introduced throw path (previously buildYandexAuthUrl touched no crypto API at all) with no caller-side protection.
findings.recommendation: Either guard with `if (!window.crypto?.getRandomValues) { /* fall back or return null */ }` before the byte-generation fallback, or wrap the AuthModal.jsx handleAuthClick body in try/catch and fail closed (no navigation) with a console log, consistent with how buildYandexAuthUrl already fails closed when VITE_YA_CLIENT_ID is missing.

findings.issue: The `request()` helper in accessApi.js (lines 6-30) duplicates ~20 lines of response-unwrapping/error-status-attaching logic that already exists nearly verbatim in panelApi.js's own `request()` (lines 3-35) — same error-message extraction, same `error.status = response.status` attachment, same empty-body-on-certain-statuses handling. The two copies have already drifted slightly (panelApi.js additionally maps 405 to "api_method_not_allowed"; accessApi.js does not).
findings.impact: Two independently-maintained copies of the same fetch-wrapping contract increase the chance that a future fix (e.g. a new empty-body status code, a new error-shape convention) gets applied to one file and not the other, silently reintroducing inconsistent error handling between the two API layers.
findings.recommendation: Extract the shared request/error-unwrapping logic into a single helper (e.g. a small `apiRequest.js` used by both panelApi.js and accessApi.js), parameterized for the small differences (204 vs 201/204 empty-body statuses, the 405 special-case).

findings.issue: hasPanelAccess() recomputes `has_access || role === 'admin'` on the client, but the server's own AccessState contract (server/api/openapi.yaml:492-494 and server/internal/handler/access.go:61-62,80) already returns `has_access` as the *final* right (has_access_raw OR role==admin) for GET /api/v1/access/me — the raw, role-unaware flag is only used in the separate UserRecord schema for the admin list endpoint. So `hasPanelAccess(accessState)`'s `|| accessState?.role === "admin"` is a no-op against the actual access/me payload: it can never flip a false to true that the server hasn't already flipped.
findings.impact: Purely cosmetic/redundant today (OR-ing an already-final boolean with a second condition is harmless), but it misrepresents the contract to future readers: a maintainer reading only Panel.jsx would reasonably (and incorrectly) conclude the server sends a raw, role-unaware has_access and that this client-side OR is load-bearing. This mismatch is explicitly instructed by the task's own implementation hints ('клиентское зеркало серверного has_access || role == admin'), so it's a spec-level redundancy rather than an implementer error, but it's still worth surfacing since it's the kind of thing that causes a future author to 'fix' the server to send the raw flag and unknowingly break this client mirror.
findings.recommendation: Either drop the client-side OR and trust access/me's has_access as already-final (simplifying hasPanelAccess to `Boolean(accessState?.has_access)`), or add a one-line comment at the AccessState definition/handleMe in access.go cross-referencing that the client intentionally re-applies the same rule defensively — pick one source of truth and say so in both places.

findings.issue: Pre-existing (not introduced by this diff, confirmed against HEAD): handleLogout's `logout().catch(() => {})` swallows any logout failure completely — no console log, no user-facing notice — before unconditionally redirecting to '/' in `.finally()`. This matches the severity-anchor pattern 'Swallowed error (catch without re-throw/log) — critical' verbatim, but it is untouched by Task 7's diff.
findings.impact: If POST /auth/logout fails server-side (network error, 5xx), the user is silently bounced to '/' with no indication their session may still be live server-side, and there is no log trail to diagnose logout failures.
findings.recommendation: Out of scope for this task's changes, but flagged because Panel.jsx is a touched file: add at least a console.log/console.error of the caught error, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in this same file (e.g. yandexAuth.js's saveAuthReturnTo/consumeAuthReturnTo `console.log(...)` pattern) so logout failures are at least visible in dev tools.

summary: No critical or major defects found. accessApi.js/AccessRequestBanner.jsx's 409-handling contract, the Panel.jsx status state-machine (checking/ready/no-access) and its two guarded data-loading effects, the AuthCallback.jsx state-mismatch abort logic (never calls exchangeYandexCode on missing/mismatched state, consumes the stored state exactly once on the code-present path), panelApi.js's userID removal (verified with grep — no stray userID references, params, or path segments anywhere in the 9 exports or their Panel.jsx call sites), and the crypto-based state generation (both randomUUID and getRandomValues paths produce adequate 128-bit CSPRNG entropy for CSRF-token purposes) all check out against the task spec and the actual server contract (openapi.yaml + access.go, read directly since server files are out of this task's scope). Build passes with VITE_YA_CLIENT_ID set, and the compiled bundle confirms scope/state and randomUUID/getRandomValues code paths are live, not dead-code-eliminated. Five minor findings: a StrictMode-induced deterministic error flash during dev-mode login testing (collides with the task's own prescribed localhost:5173 verification flow), a missing window.crypto existence guard on the getRandomValues fallback with no caller-side try/catch, duplicated request/error-wrapping logic between accessApi.js and panelApi.js, a redundant (but harmless, spec-mandated) client-side re-derivation of has_access that the server already finalizes, and a pre-existing (not introduced by this task) swallowed error in handleLogout. The three self-disclosed deviations (private saveAuthState, crypto fallback, reused .panel__theme-toggle button class) are all sound: saveAuthState's non-export creates no coupling issue since buildYandexAuthUrl is genuinely the only legitimate writer; the crypto fallback is cryptographically adequate on both paths (minus the missing existence guard noted above); and .panel__theme-toggle is already the codebase's de facto primary-action-button style (reused for both the theme toggle and the 'Рассчитать' submit button elsewhere in the same file), so reusing it for the access-request button is consistent with existing practice, not a new semantic mismatch.
